consensus_summary: The consensus identifies the core symbolism as irreversible, total divine judgment or destruction, where the sinking object is permanently removed. While judgment is the primary meaning (especially for cities or individuals), it is also commonly seen as representing the removal of sins or the overcoming of obstacles through faith.
book_summary: The book narrows the symbol exclusively to the fall of Babylon—representing a ruling power being irreversibly destroyed and sinking into the 'sea of peoples' to never rise again.
consensus_core_identification: Irreversible divine destruction, judgment, or removal of an entity (person, city, sin, or obstacle).
book_core_identification: The irreversible destruction of a ruling power (Babylon) sinking into the sea of peoples.
boundary_disagreement: The book excludes broader applications of the imagery, such as individual judgment for causing someone to stumble (Matthew 18:6), the removal of sin (Micah 7:19), or faith overcoming obstacles (Mark 11:23). It confines the symbol strictly to the apocalyptic and prophetic destruction of a ruling political power.
material_contradiction: None. The book affirms the core consensus concept of 'irreversible destruction' but tightly restricts its scope to a specific referent (a ruling power) and interprets the 'sea' specifically as the 'sea of peoples'.
rationale: The book selects one specific strand of the consensus (the destruction of a kingdom/Babylon, explicitly noted in the consensus alternatives) and makes it the exclusive definition, narrowing both the core referent and the applicable extension.
strongest_objection: By restricting this phrase-symbol entirely to 'the fall of Babylon / a ruling power,' the book neglects identical phrasing in the gospels regarding individuals (the millstone warning) and faith (casting mountains into the sea), which use the same imagery for different applications.
